general.title: DNS Propagation: What Actually Happens After You Change a Record
general.describe: You change an A record, and your phone loads the new server while your laptop keeps loading the old one. DNS has no mechanism for pushing a change out to resolvers. What people call propagation is resolvers everywhere holding cached copies of the old answer until each copy's TTL runs out. This guide shows where those copies live, how to inspect each one with dig , and a migration order that keeps the switchover short and reversible.
